data.name: Muwahhid
data.gender_notes: Muwahhid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'w-h-d', meaning 'one' or 'unique'. Signifies belief in the oneness of God. The name Muwahhid carries the meaning “One God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muwahhid usually hope their child will grow to embody one god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A person who has dedicated their life to the worship of Allah and the belief in the oneness of God
data.etymology: Muwahhid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muwahhid total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: موحد
in_arabic.meaning: من يؤكد وحدة الله تعالى ويشهد بالتوحيد
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من توحيد، وهو الإقرار بوحدة الله تعالى وعدم وجود شريك له. يدل على إيمان قوي واعتراف بالتوحيد الخالص. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الإخلاص: 'قل هو الله أحد * الله الصمد * لم يلد ولم يولد * ولم يكن له كفوا أحد' (الإخلاص: 1-4).

in_urdu.name: موحد
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو اللہ کی وحدانیت کا اقرار کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: موحد وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو اللہ تعالیٰ کی وحدانیت کو مانتا ہے اور اس کی یگانہ پرستی کا اقرار کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں 'توحید' کا مطلب ہے 'اللہ کی وحدانیت'۔ اسلامی روایت میں اس نام کا بڑا احترام ہے کیونکہ یہ توحید کے اصول پر زور دیتا ہے، جو اسلامی عقیدے کا بنیادی ستون ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुवाहीद
in_hindi.meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो ईश्वर की एकता को स्वीकार करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुवाहीद वह व्यक्ति होता है जो ईश्वर की एकता को स्वीकार करता है और उसकी अद्वैतता का प्रमाण देता है। यह नाम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है, जहां 'तौहीद' का अर्थ है 'ईश्वर की एकता'। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का विशेष महत्व है क्योंकि यह तौहीद के सिद्धांत पर बल देता है, जो इस्लामी विश्वास का मूल आधार है।

in_pashto.name: موحد
in_pashto.meaning: هغه کسان چې د الله یووالي مني
in_pashto.long_meaning: موحد هغه څوک دی چې د الله تعالی یووالي ومني او د هغه د یووالي شاهدی ورکوي. دا نوم د عربي ريښو څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چیرته چې 'توحید' معنی د 'الله یووالي'. په افغان او پښتون دود کې دې نوم ډیر احترام ورته کیږي ځکه چې د توحید په اصل باندې ټینګار کوي، کوم چې د اسلامي عقیدې بنیادی ستون دی.

in_english.name: Muwahhid
in_english.meaning: One who affirms the oneness of God
in_english.long_meaning: Muwahhid is derived from the Arabic root 'wahhada', meaning 'to affirm the oneness'. It refers to someone who acknowledges and declares the unity of God, a fundamental concept in Islam known as Tawhid. This name holds significant spiritual and theological importance as it underscores the central belief in Islamic monotheism. Historically, the term has been used to describe those who strongly advocate for the oneness of God, free from any form of polytheism or idolatry.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Tumart and the Almohad Caliphate (1121-1163) The name Muwahhid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Tumart, a Berber scholar from the region of the Djadid in Morocco, preached the idea of Tawhid, the oneness of God. His followers, known as the Almohads, adopted this name, which means 'unitarians' in Arabic. Ibn Tumart established a new Islamic state in 1121, which grew rapidly under the military leadership of his disciple, Abd al-Mu'min. The Almohad empire became a major power in the Western Islamic world, extending from the Iberian Peninsula to the Maghreb.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sultan al-Muwahhid of the Marinids (1310-1331) The name Muwahhid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Marinids were a Berber dynasty from the Rif Mountains in Morocco, who established their power in the Maghreb during the 13th century. Sultan Abu Yahya Abul Hassan Ali ibn Omar, known as Sultan al-Muwahhid, ruled the Marinid empire from 1310 to 1331. He was a learned man, a poet, and a patron of scholars and artists. The name 'Muwahhid' means 'unitarian' in Arabic, reflecting the Marinid dynasty's adherence to the doctrine of Tawhid, the oneness of God.
